title: Judgment extension v1 (PROVISIONAL)
description: PROVISIONAL, held for ratification; not registered, not normative. Companion schema for the Agent Action Capsule judgment extension: a Capsule that records a judgment (by an AI judge or a human expert) over an evidence set. The extension adds only what the base profile lacks -- rubric_digest, rubric_version, judge_parameters_digest, and for a model judge model_hosting with optional model_reference and model_digest -- in one namespaced member at /model_attestation/compute_attestation/x-judgment-v1. Base fields keep their meaning: developer = the judge (model and version, or a non-identifying rater role label), compute_attestation.agent_output_digest = JSON-DIGEST of the judge's answer {verdict, rationale}, references[] = exactly one citation_purpose judged_from naming the evidence set by digest. The binding makes a judgment re-runnable, not reproducible: a verifier never re-runs a model; it recomputes digests from published preimages. The digest rules for rubric_digest and judge_parameters_digest stated in the $defs below are PROPOSED and UNRATIFIED (see vectors/judgment/README.md). How each member corresponds to a pack's judge declaration is stated in spec/judgment-extension-v1.md. The root validates a judgment Capsule as an overlay: it constrains only the members this extension relies on and leaves every other Capsule member to the base profile's own Class 1 checks.

JudgmentMember.description: The extension member, carried at /model_attestation/compute_attestation/x-judgment-v1. Closed: an extra member is a schema failure, so a later revision adds members by a new versioned member name, never silently.

rubric_digest.description: PROPOSED rule: JSON-DIGEST (lowercase-hex SHA-256 of UTF8(JCS(value)), no member filtering) of one published rubric document (RubricDocument). The digest covers the whole document value.

rubric_version.description: The producer's human label for the rubric, verbatim. A label, never identity: two records with equal rubric_version and different rubric_digest were judged against two different rubrics.

judge_parameters_digest.description: PROPOSED rule: JSON-DIGEST of the published judge-parameters object -- JudgeParameters for a model judge, ExpertProtocolParameters for a human expert. Excludes the judge's identity, which developer carries, and model_hosting, which this member carries.

model_hosting.description: PROPOSED. Where the model named by developer ran, over the same closed set a pack's judge declaration uses. hosted: reached through another party's endpoint whose weights the producer does not hold and whose model can change without its name changing; the verdict is attributable, not re-derivable. self_hosted: the producer runs the weights; whether they are published is not stated here. Outside judge_parameters_digest (it describes the judge, not how the judge was asked); committed by capsule_id like every member. A model-judge record MUST carry it; a human-expert record MUST NOT. A verifier that finds it absent on a model-judge record treats the judgment as hosted. See spec/judgment-extension-v1.md.

model_reference.description: PROPOSED, OPTIONAL. Identity rung 2: a reference naming one model artifact (for example repository, revision and file). It proves which artifact was named, not which bytes were loaded. Absent when the producer has no such reference; never an empty or placeholder string. See spec/judgment-extension-v1.md, Model identity ladder.

model_digest.description: PROPOSED, OPTIONAL. Identity rung 3: lowercase-hex SHA-256 over the raw bytes of the model file actually loaded to produce this judgment. Self-reported: it makes the judgment re-derivable in principle, not proven. Absent when not computed or not computable -- never a zero, an empty string or a placeholder; the all-zero value is rejected. Requires model_hosting, and MUST NOT accompany model_hosting hosted: nobody outside a hosted endpoint holds the loaded bytes. See spec/judgment-extension-v1.md, Model identity ladder.

Reference.description: A references[] entry: a CPB typed digest reference with a citation purpose. Digest is identity.

JudgedFromReference.description: Matches a references[] entry whose citation_purpose is judged_from (pending registration). The target is the evidence set the judgment was made from: a Capsule's capsule_id, an Evidence Bundle digest, or a composed/v1 composed digest.

JudgmentCapsule.description: Overlay on an Agent Action Capsule carrying the judgment extension. Requires: developer; model_attestation.compute_attestation with agent_output_digest and the x-judgment-v1 member; references[] containing exactly one judged_from entry. Other Capsule members are not constrained here.

developer.description: Base field. The judge. For a model judge: model_id, or model_id "@" version, where model_id is the model identifier exactly as a pack's judge declaration names it (byte-equal, no normalization) and contains no "@". For a human expert: a role or pseudonymous rater label -- never a personal name or contact identifier. See spec/judgment-extension-v1.md, Model identity.

agent_output_digest.description: Base field. JSON-DIGEST of the judge's answer object (JudgeAnswer).

references.description: Exactly one judged_from entry. Other entries (for example calibrated_against, pending registration) are allowed.

JudgeAnswer.description: Preimage of agent_output_digest. verdict uses the Evidence Contract's three-value vocabulary. This definition is the answer schema of every x-judgment-v1 record: a pack's judge declaration that pins an answer schema hash for a judge recorded under this member pins JSON-DIGEST of this definition's value as published in this file (spec/judgment-extension-v1.md, Answer schema).

RubricDocument.description: Preimage of rubric_digest: the rubric as published, digested whole. Content is producer-defined. When the judge reads reference text (a policy document), the rubric SHOULD carry policy_digest so that text is bound too. Floats are forbidden, as in every digest-bearing value.

policy_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes of the reference text the judge reads.

SamplingParams.description: Sampling parameters as sent to the judge model. Integers, strings and booleans only: no floats (a fractional temperature is a decimal string, or an integer in micros).

JudgeParameters.description: Preimage of judge_parameters_digest for a model judge: everything about how the judge was asked, except the model (developer carries it). Inner *_digest members are SHA-256 of raw file bytes (prompt_digest, axes_digest) or JSON-DIGEST of a JSON value (instruction_template_digest).

instruction_template_digest.description: JSON-DIGEST of the instruction template object the judge code wraps around the rubric and the evidence, as published, before anything is interpolated into it. An interpolated prompt carries the action's content and never enters this preimage. This is the digest a pack's judge declaration pins as its prompt template hash (spec/judgment-extension-v1.md).

prompt_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes of the published judge prompt file. A published artifact, never an interpolated prompt. Not a template-object digest: a pack's prompt template hash never equals this value, even where an implementation calls its own template digest prompt_digest (spec/judgment-extension-v1.md).

axes_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes of the published axes file.

min_confidence_micros.description: Confidence floor in micros (0..1000000) below which the judge's verdict is reported as not_evaluable.

judge_batch.description: Number of cases sent to the judge in one request. Batching changes the request the model sees.

ExpertProtocolParameters.description: Preimage of judge_parameters_digest for a human expert: the rating protocol and the packet the rater was shown.

packet_digest.description: JSON-DIGEST of the packet shown to the rater.
